grounds: the failing path is byte-identical to H2a's: process_snapshot_linux.go's linuxProcessResidentBytes, collectLinuxResidentObservation and smaps_rollup handling all date to commit 059e6616 and this slice changed none of them; the ten lines this slice removed from that file are exactly the inline census block, and f5347398's change to it was confined to error classification inside readLinuxProcessCensus, leaving the happy path byte-identical

the mechanism is a deliberate race the test constructs: it launches /bin/sh -c '/bin/sh -c "sleep 1; exec /usr/bin/git hash-object --stdin" child <&3 & wait' and polls every 20ms for the other-to-git exec transition, so the sampler walks the tree at the instant sleep 1 exits. A descendant that exits is simultaneously reparented, which breaks the parent-equality half of linuxProcessResidentBytes' zero-RSS recovery condition and turns a missing smaps_rollup into the hard error; collectLinuxResidentObservation retries only errLinuxProcessNameTransition, and the test's own table pins {'missing memory', os.ErrNotExist, 'name', 1, true}

newly_named_prerequisite.name: Linux immutable-flag input-custody model
newly_named_prerequisite.finding: Linux FS_IMMUTABLE_FL via FS_IOC_SETFLAGS requires CAP_LINUX_IMMUTABLE; there is no unprivileged owner-set immutable equivalent to Darwin's unix.Fchflags(UF_IMMUTABLE). inputCustodyOwned, inputCustodyProtected, inputCustodyFlag and inputCustodyVolume are therefore refusal stubs on Linux, and ProtectExecutionGoBuildInputs plus the whole zoekt-offer native build path cannot run here.
newly_named_prerequisite.why_it_matters: it is a genuine design question rather than a port: the options are a granted capability, a read-only bind mount, a user namespace, or an explicitly weaker documented custody model, and each has a different adversary.
newly_named_prerequisite.backlog_status: was not named in the remaining-H2-prerequisites list before this slice; it is now recorded in docs/BACKLOG.md under T42.H2f and T42.H2g.

cost_pass: No new per-query/request, sync tick, startup/restart, retry/no-op or publication work; ordinary runtime is unchanged and no production dispatch site is added or removed. The changed path is supervision-only and runs at the existing ten-millisecond poll cadence and five-second custody-command deadline. Per poll the syscall order is unchanged while one child process, one pipe and one 128-KiB text parse are removed and the two-second probe context disappears because no child bounds it: the loop is bounded by construction at maxProcessSnapshotRows = 8192 listing entries, at most 8192 getsid calls of roughly 200ns each, and at most maxProcessSessionMembers = 1024 session members each costing one /proc/<pid>/stat read plus one confirming getsid. Those are two different budgets and the da566ff3 comment conflated them: the 8192 figure is the per-host-PID getsid sweep, while the 1024 figure bounds only the members that already matched the session, and a typical private session matches zero to two PIDs. Reading /proc/<pid>/stat field 6 instead of getsid was rejected on cost, at two to five microseconds per candidate versus roughly 200 nanoseconds, over every host PID at ten milliseconds. No numeric sort was added because order is not load-bearing in any of the three callers and the Darwin census is unsorted too; the empty census now returns an empty non-nil slice rather than nil, and all three callers are nil-insensitive. f5347398 added no steady-state cost: the close-error change is on an existing error path, the bound is a named constant with the same value, and privateServerSessionPIDsAt is a test seam the production caller reaches through one non-capturing delegate. No lock is held across the census, no new persistent state exists, and no cache is invalidated.
